summary: Neither agent host expands variables in its environment block, so a workspace cannot record a HOME-relative toolchain location in host wiring the way it records the board identity.

cost: One full design pass discarded; the mechanism named in the item body cannot work and had to be replaced with BASH_ENV, which bash expands itself.

summary: Claude Code silently reverts PATH for every shell call: each call runs source <shell-snapshot> then the command, and the snapshot's last line re-exports the host process PATH, so a BASH_ENV prepend is undone while other exported variables survive.
evidence: command:grep -n 'export PATH' ~/.claude/shell-snapshots/*.sh # one match, the final line;command:claude -p 'run: printenv FSGG_AGENT_ENV_APPLIED; command -v dotnet' # marker set, muxer still the wrong one;file:scripts/agent-env.sh
cost: A fix whose synthesized-environment checks were entirely green failed in a real host session; found only because the end-to-end run was done through the actual runtime rather than a reproduction of it.

summary: For an environment fix, running every check inside env -i with bash --noprofile --norc, plus a negative control and a delete-the-mechanism mutation, is what separates a real fix from one that only works in the author's already-repaired shell.
evidence: file:docs/workspace-onboarding.md;command:env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=/usr/share/dotnet:/usr/bin:/bin DOTNET_ROOT=/usr/share/dotnet bash --noprofile --norc -c 'cd . && dotnet --version' # red without the wiring, green with it
